excerpt: Fireworks AI runs and fine-tunes open AI models for developers. GPU and fine-tuning prices, its $250M Series C, and alternatives such as Together AI and Groq.
content:
Fireworks AI is an inference platform: it runs open and custom AI models on its own GPU infrastructure so that developers can call them through an API instead of hosting them. It offers three ways to use it. Serverless inference is self-serve, paid with prepaid credits and billed by usage. On-demand deployments rent dedicated GPUs by the minute for a model of your choice. And training lets you fine-tune models, either through a managed service or a serverless training API. Larger customers can contact sales for enterprise deployments with higher rate limits.

Fireworks says its founders left the PyTorch team in 2022 to start the company, drawing on their experience scaling AI infrastructure at Meta. Customers it names include Samsung, Uber, DoorDash, Notion, Shopify and Upwork.

Funding and scale

On 28 October 2025 Fireworks announced a $250 million Series C at a $4 billion valuation, co-led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Index Ventures and Evantic, with Sequoia Capital continuing to invest. The round included primary and secondary funding and brought total funding to more than $327 million; earlier rounds were led by Benchmark and Sequoia, and NVIDIA, AMD, MongoDB and Databricks have backed it strategically. In the same post Fireworks said it powers more than 10,000 companies, processes more than 10 trillion tokens a day and has passed $280 million in annualised revenue. Those are the company's own figures.

Pricing

Per-token prices for chat models are listed in Fireworks' documentation rather than on its pricing page. The pricing page does list dedicated GPUs: an H100 or H200 costs $8.00 an hour ($0.134 a minute), a B200 $13.00 an hour, a B300 $15.00 and a GB300 $20.00, with a 1.5x premium for region-restricted deployments. Embedding models start at $0.008 per million input tokens for models up to 150 million parameters. Managed fine-tuning is priced per million training tokens by model size: LoRA supervised fine-tuning costs $0.50 for models up to 16 billion parameters, $3.00 up to 80 billion, $6.00 up to 300 billion and $10.00 above that, with full fine-tuning and DPO costing more.

We have not tested Fireworks AI ourselves. This page brings together Fireworks AI's official site, its own announcements and reputable news coverage, plus the public pages of the products it is compared with, and says where each fact comes from.

Rent dedicated GPUs by the minute for a custom model

fit: are an engineering team building on open-weight models and want someone else to run the GPUs
need dedicated capacity billed by the minute
want fine-tuning and serving from the same provider
not_fit: only need one closed model such as GPT or Claude; call that provider directly
want a flat monthly subscription: everything is usage-based
are not technical: this is an API platform for developers

pros: Published per-hour GPU prices billed by the minute
Serving, fine-tuning and embeddings in one platform
Named customers at scale (Samsung, Uber, Notion, Shopify)
cons: Chat-model token prices are in the docs, not on the pricing page

pricing.intro: Fireworks AI's own prices, in US dollars. Serverless chat-model token prices are in its documentation.

plans.name: Serverless inference
plans.detail: Self-serve; per-token prices per model in the docs. Embeddings from $0.008 per 1M input tokens

plans.name: On-demand GPUs
plans.detail: H100 or H200 $8.00/hr, B200 $13.00/hr, B300 $15.00/hr, GB300 $20.00/hr, billed per minute

plans.name: Managed fine-tuning
plans.detail: LoRA SFT: $0.50 (up to 16B), $3.00 (to 80B), $6.00 (to 300B), $10.00 (over 300B); full fine-tuning and DPO cost more

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: Faster speeds, lower costs and higher rate limits

notes: Fireworks advertised free supervised fine-tuning of its Muse Glimmer 30B model until 31 October; check whether that offer still runs.

alternatives.intro: Other inference platforms for open models. Descriptions come from each company's own site; check their pricing pages for current rates.

items.name: Together AI
items.what: AI cloud for inference, fine-tuning and GPU clusters
items.difference: Similar scope; also rents GPU clusters for training.

items.name: Groq
items.what: Neocloud for fast inference on its own integrated platform
items.difference: Runs on its own chips and focuses on speed.

items.name: Baseten
items.what: Inference platform for serving open-source and custom AI models in production
items.difference: Strong focus on deploying your own custom models.

faq.a: An inference platform that runs open and custom AI models for developers through an API, with dedicated GPUs and fine-tuning available.

faq.q: How much does Fireworks AI cost?
faq.a: It is usage-based. Dedicated H100 or H200 GPUs cost $8.00 an hour, billed by the minute; LoRA fine-tuning starts at $0.50 per million training tokens; per-token model prices are in its docs.

faq.q: How much has Fireworks AI raised?
faq.a: It announced a $250 million Series C at a $4 billion valuation on 28 October 2025, bringing total funding to more than $327 million.
Fireworks says its founders left the PyTorch team in 2022 to start the company, after scaling AI infrastructure at Meta.
It names Samsung, Uber, DoorDash, Notion, Shopify and Upwork, and says it powers more than 10,000 companies.
